decisions.reason: A hearty bread loaf sits at the core of the firm's traditional bakery range, costs little to keep, and was visibly presented over several years, so management stays with it.
The sweet pastry fits the firm's heritage confectionery identity, and any weak sales can be blamed on temporary pandemic disruption rather than on the product itself.
A crusty farmhouse bread is close to the established offer and the firm's announced craft-tradition direction, so dropping it would contradict earlier commitments for little gain.
The gold-awarded poppy seed stollen has its own website page and carries public prestige, so management is strongly committed to continuing it.
The premium stollen won a gold award and is publicly promoted as a seasonal flagship, which strongly favours keeping it.
